summary: Completed Phase 1 (kernel), Phase 1.5 (sync), and Phase 2 (skills) in a single session. 76 files created, 168 tests passing. All 12 seed commands operational.
lessons: Bootstrap session needs kernel write protection temporarily disabled — use Python script to toggle, not sed
Sync pipeline should run BEFORE manual skill creation to avoid duplicate work
Seed commands should be created alongside the phases they serve, not deferred

summary: The sync tool preserves source directory paths (.agents/skills/) rather than remapping to target paths (skills/). This creates a dual-location issue where synced and hand-written skills live in different directories.
lessons: Sync tool needs a path_mapping config for source-to-target directory remapping
Architecture should decide: use source paths or Azoth paths as canonical

summary: Decided to hand-write all 8 core skills rather than extract via sync. The 5 'extracted' skills were authored from patterns observed in source framework commands, not directly copied. This produced cleaner, Azoth-native skills but bypassed the sync workflow.
lessons: Hand-writing produces better-adapted skills but is slower and doesn't validate the sync pipeline
Future skill additions should use sync-then-adapt workflow: extract via sync, then refine for Azoth conventions

goal: Deliver bootstrap PR and set up GitHub CLI
summary: gh CLI was not installed and Homebrew was absent. Installed gh directly via versioned zip to ~/.local/bin (already in PATH). This avoided sudo requirement entirely. PR created cleanly without co-authored-by in body.
lessons: Direct binary install to ~/.local/bin works when Homebrew/sudo unavailable — check PATH first before assuming package manager needed
Co-authored-by lines in PR bodies are unwanted — omit from gh pr create --body even when present in commits

summary: 4 insights from supplygrowth-architect were triaged and archived. All 4 were stale — each issue had already been resolved by the personal scaffold work done during the bootstrap session before the audit was captured. insight-001: strip_patterns was empty → already populated. insight-002: agentic-eval drift → both files now 219 lines. insight-003: azoth.yaml missing scope fields → already added. insight-004: no external intake channel in GOVERNANCE.md → Section 7 already written.
lessons: Cross-project audits can lag behind active development — always verify evidence before integrating
The bootstrap session moved fast enough that audit-time state was already resolved by triage-time

summary: Settings template denies Edit(kernel/**) but not Edit(.azoth/kernel/**) — deployed kernel files in consumer projects are unprotected against agent edits.
recommended_action: Add Edit(.azoth/kernel/**) to the deny list in settings.json.template

summary: ACTIVATE phase references kernel/ paths but installer deploys to .azoth/kernel/ — boot instructions break in consumer projects.
recommended_action: Make ACTIVATE references path-agnostic or document scaffold vs installed paths explicitly

summary: Drift detection example hashes kernel/*.md but installed projects use .azoth/kernel/*.md — documented integrity check will fail in consumer projects.
recommended_action: Update sha256sum command to .azoth/kernel/*.md or document both scaffold and installed paths

summary: Integrity check examples reference kernel/BOOTLOADER.md etc — wrong paths for consumer projects where kernel lives under .azoth/kernel/.
recommended_action: Update sha256sum examples to .azoth/kernel/ or document both scaffold and installed layouts

summary: read_text() calls lack encoding parameter — will raise UnicodeDecodeError on Windows where default encoding is not UTF-8.
recommended_action: Change all read_text() calls to read_text(encoding="utf-8") for cross-platform portability

summary: Hardcodes D1-D28 but repo now tracks D1-D41 — evaluation criteria is stale.
recommended_action: Update to D1-D41 or reference docs/DECISIONS_INDEX.md dynamically

summary: Hardcodes D1-D28 — same stale reference as pr-review-006.
State schema shows active_phase: 1 (integer) but template uses active_phase: operate (string enum) — type mismatch between docs and runtime.

summary: AZOTH_PHASE is 1.5-complete in settings.json, phase: 3 in azoth.yaml, and operate in template — three conflicting values across three sources.

summary: Root cause of pr-review-002/003/004: systemic path duality (kernel/ in scaffold, .azoth/kernel/ in consumer) is undocumented as an architecture decision. All three kernel docs assume scaffold paths.
recommended_action: Create D42 documenting path duality convention; add Path Convention section to BOOTLOADER.md; update all kernel docs with dual-path awareness

goal: Establish external PR review → governed intake pipeline
summary: Successfully ran the Copilot PR review → inbox → intake → M3 workflow end-to-end for the first time. Two intake passes: one stale batch (4 archived), one live batch (10 integrated). The workflow proves the governance loop works across tool boundaries — external agents can feed M3 without bypassing human triage.
lessons: Copilot PR review can generate structured insight files that conform to the intake schema — this is a repeatable workflow
Always verify evidence before integrating: stale audits are a real failure mode when dev pace exceeds audit cadence
Systemic root-cause insights (like D42 path duality) are more valuable than the individual bug reports they subsume — flag and elevate them

summary: Agent definitions written in two passes: v1 as metadata cards (64 lines avg), then enriched with behavioral depth from 16 source framework agents (122 lines avg). Key extraction: subagent contracts, concrete protocols with output formats, quality scoring rubrics, anti-patterns. Source agents lived in .github/agents/ which the sync tool doesn't scan — manual extraction was required. The /auto pipeline (classify → planner → test-builder → builder → architect-review) ran successfully end-to-end.
lessons: Agent definitions must be written as system prompts ('You are...') with concrete protocols, not as metadata descriptions — the source framework's production agents prove this
Sync tool's SYNCABLE_PARENT_DIRS doesn't include .github/agents/ — manual extraction is needed for Copilot-format agent definitions
The /auto pipeline classification correctly routes additive agent work to the deliver pipeline — validates D23 composition rules
Test-first development caught a .stem vs .removesuffix bug in drift detection — TDD works even for definition files
Two-pass approach (scaffold then enrich) is more effective than trying to write final-quality agents in one pass — similar to the sync-then-adapt pattern from ep-003

goal: Evaluate research timing vs session closeout
summary: User asked whether to run Claude Code multi-agent orchestration research now or close out first. Decided to close out: context window was heavily loaded (2 pipelines + extensive source reading), deliverables uncommitted, and the research topic (Claude Code platform integration) belongs to P3-002/Phase 4, not P3-001. Existing external analyses (22+38 sources, quality 0.92+0.84) already cover the landscape well enough to inform next session's planning.
lessons: Session discipline matters — close out when deliverables are ready rather than expanding scope
External research reports are a high-value asset — read them before spawning new research
Platform integration research (how agents map to Claude Code AgentTool/Skills/Hooks) is a distinct task from agent definition
